note: Missouri River bottomland west of Watson, a Corps mitigation tract managed by MDC, in two parts: the north tract is reached only by boat, and the camping is on the south tract. MDC's one primitive camping area is beside the gravel parking lot at the end of Aurora Avenue, just inside the levee, among brush and young cottonwoods. No pads and no facilities; the bottoms flood. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: the one map/GIS-designated primitive camping area (GIS 391) is on the drivable SOUTH tract beside the lot at the end of Aurora Avenue, not the boat-only north tract. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches; not waterfront kept; pin is in brush - move 61 m onto the lot.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Designated Camping Sites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map' and 'Public access to the north tract is by boat only from the Missouri and Nishnabotna Rivers'; the map (© 05/16) labels the north tract 'Boat Access Only' and draws its one 'Primitive Camping Area' symbol beside the one Parking Lot on the south tract at the end of Aurora St; GIS 27 point 391, GIS 26 lot 3259. Rule 140 standard; no special-use-only rule, no Rule 101. A designated point at a lot edge (kept, as Lick Creek).

PIN (61 m move out of the brush): stored 40.46020,-95.66539 = GIS 391, which on leaf-on imagery falls in dense brush and saplings with no track to it. Lot 3259 (40.45980,-95.66589) is a ~25 x 12 m gravel lot at the end of the gravel spur off the levee road, with a mown margin around it; suggested pin 40.45980,-95.66589. The stored pin is already on the south tract (the brief's question): the north tract is ~3 km NNW.

ACCESS: page directions 'To reach the south tract, from Watson take Route A west 2 miles, continue west on gravel road 175th Street 0.50 mile then take Aurora Ave south 0.75 mile to the area.' Gravel, flat, over the federal levee; no ford, no 4WD wording. Missouri River floodplain - subject to flooding (no closure posted on the page today).
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. The lot is ~500 m from the Missouri River behind the levee and timber; the old chute east of it is not in view from the lot.
HORSES: brochure 'Bicycles, horses, and horseback riding are allowed only on roads open to vehicles.' No horse camp. CLUSTERS: one spot.
The page gives 2,435.6 acres; the 05/16 map says 2,907.
